label: about link
defaultValue: about this experiment

label: about — introduction
defaultValue:
this experiment grew out of conversations about the kinds of work we do, the assumptions, values and logics they operate within, and what makes different ways of working possible.

we're curious to explore the relationship between how deeply our work reproduces, questions or transforms dominant ways of organising, and how well that work sustains our livelihoods.

label: about — research context
defaultValue:
by inviting people to place themselves on this map, we hope to gather perspectives that reveal patterns, contradictions and questions worth exploring further.

there are no right answers. this is an exploratory inquiry, not a representative study, and each placement reflects someone's own experience and interpretation.

this experiment is part of research into the political economy of transition: how power, ownership and resources shape the possibilities for doing work differently.

question 6 uses the wording of the EU-SILC survey, so answers can be compared with danish and european figures. this provides a point of comparison; these self-selected responses are not representative of the wider population.

label: privacy — what is collected

label: privacy — access and publication
defaultValue: full individual submissions are accessible only to the researcher through the private research page. if you opt in above, your coordinates and, with separate permission, your work or situation can also be seen by respondents viewing the shared map. your situation, country of work, difference dimensions and other written and financial answers are not shown on that map. findings may be shared in aggregate, with any quoted descriptions de-identified.

label: privacy — storage and retention

label: framework image — accessible description
defaultValue: Hypothesised relationship between what work affords and how fundamentally it departs from dominant systems. Work-derived material security and financial surplus runs from precarious through getting by and secure to substantial surplus. The four regions are structural advantage, systemic precarity, transformative precarity and transformative viability. A descending current tendency is a hypothesis, not observed results.
